lyrics:
There's a mad man in the people's house
There's a mad man in the people's house
He has the key. He's past the gate
He only sleeps by mistake
Cannot keep the mad man in the house

There's a mad man in a broken pool
There's a mad man in a broken pool

And when his rage comes thundering through the halls

And the shouting is the only thing we hear
Some day there'll be a January to cheer

There's a mad man in the cabinet room
There's a mad man in the cabinet room

And when his rage comes thundering through the halls
And the minders on the hill have gone to ground
And the shouting is the only thing we hear

We watched the doors swing open

review.review_text: 4Castle has been circling political dread for a while, but this is the first time they've aimed the lens this directly at a specific kind of power, and the restraint makes it hit harder than a screed would. The verses build their case with dry economy: 'He only sleeps by mistake,' 'the deep end's dry, the tiles are cold,' images that feel absurdist and precise at the same time, the way good political writing does when it trusts the audience. The chorus lands in E major at a brisk 136 BPM, the harmony vocals opening up the room right when the lyric needs the feeling of collective exhalation, and the Hammond on rotary pushes it into something that recalls late-period Traffic or the more purposeful end of prog-rock civics. The spoken interlude, a quietly mumbling figure congratulating himself on being 'better than that,' is the sharpest move on the track, unsettling precisely because it sounds bored and sincere rather than theatrical. The final chorus earns its single-word substitution: 'rage goes quiet,' 'stood their ground,' traffic instead of shouting, ordinary life returned. That pivot is the whole argument, and 4Castle makes it without flinching.
